questions.heading: The Fixed LP Prices Only What Stayed Free
questions.stem: A depot MILP decides which of 12 vans to lease, yes or no each, and has no continuous variables. An analyst fixes the chosen vans, re-solves the LP and reports the fuel-budget row's dual value. What will it be, and why?

options.text: The best van's value per dollar, since that van is the marginal lease
options.says: With every van fixed no lease can change, so no van is marginal in the fixed LP.

options.text: The LP relaxation's price, since fixing the vans leaves the duals as they were
options.says: Fixing changes the LP: the relaxation's fractional vans are gone, and so is their price.

options.text: Zero, since with every van fixed nothing is left for money to buy
options.says: Right: a fixed-integer price prices only what stayed free, and here nothing did.

options.text: Undefined, since a fixed LP has no dual solution of its own
options.says: The fixed LP is an LP and has duals; lesson 5.3.2's prices were all 0, not missing.

questions.heading: Binding Means Zero Slack; a Binding Row Can Still Have a Zero Price
questions.stem: A fixed-integer LP's report lists the row permit_R4 with slack 0 and dual value 0. A reviewer wants it taken off the list of binding rows. What is right?

options.text: Keep it: zero slack makes it binding; a bound can carry the price
options.says: Right: binding means zero slack; in a degenerate LP the price can be carried by a variable's bound.

options.text: Take it off: in an LP a binding row always carries a nonzero dual value
options.says: must_P003 bound with a price of 0, so a binding row need not carry a price.

options.text: Take it off: a zero dual value means the solver ignored the row
options.says: The row holds with equality at the plan; the solver did not ignore it.

options.text: Keep it: every row of a fixed-integer LP binds once the plan is fixed
options.says: clearance_cap had slack 800 in the fixed LP, so not every row binds.

questions.heading: The Price Holds Only With the Plan Fixed and Inside Its Range
questions.stem: A fixed-integer LP prices a fuel budget at 0.4 per $k. In the plan, a continuous purchase of spot fuel sits at 0, its lower bound, well below its cap of 300. Finance asks about a $100k cut and a $100k increase. Which can you state?

options.text: Both: the MILP loses 40 on the cut and gains 40 on the increase
options.says: With spot fuel at 0 the cut cannot be absorbed, and the MILP may gain more than 40 by re-choosing.

options.text: The cut: the MILP loses at most 40; the increase is unknown
options.says: The cut is the side the price cannot speak to: the fixed plan becomes infeasible.

options.text: Neither: a fixed-integer price never says anything about the MILP
options.says: Inside its range, for an increase, the price is a floor on the MILP's gain.

options.text: The increase: the MILP gains at least 40; the cut is unknown
options.says: Right: the fixed plan plus 100 of spot fuel is still a plan, so the gain is at least 40; a cut has no room.
